title: Chelsea Buns
subtitle: Spiralled yeasted buns with currants and brown sugar
excerpt: A British bakery classic from the Chelsea Bun House: soft, enriched dough rolled out, spread with butter and brown sugar, scattered with currants, then cut into spirals and baked close together in a tin so they pull apart at the table.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chelsea buns originated at the Chelsea Bun House on the King's Road, a bakery that operated from around 1700 until 1839 and became one of the most famous baking establishments in Britain. The buns were reported to draw enormous crowds on Good Friday, with queues stretching the length of the King's Road. Members of the royal family including King George III and George IV were documented customers. The defining characteristic of the Chelsea bun is the rolled-and-cut method that produces the swirled layers of fruit and sugar, and the fact that the buns are baked touching each other in a square tin so they merge during baking and are pulled apart by hand when serving.

recipeTools.notes: A 23 cm square tin, greased and lined.

content.text: Roll the dough into a rectangle about 30 by 23 cm before adding the filling: the thickness determines the size of the spirals in the finished bun. Leave a 2 cm border along one long edge so the roll seals properly. Roll tightly and evenly so each bun has a uniform spiral. Place them cut-side up, touching each other in the tin.

items.preparation: in the dough, softened; plus 30 g for the filling

content.text: Mix the flour, yeast, caster sugar, and salt. Rub in 25 g butter. Add the warm milk and egg and mix to a soft dough. Knead for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour until doubled.

Knock back the dough and roll into a 30 by 23 cm rectangle. Spread with 30 g of softened butter. Mix the brown sugar, currants, cinnamon, and orange zest and scatter evenly over the dough. Roll up from a long edge into a tight log. Cut into 9 equal rounds (about 3 cm thick) and place cut-side up in the greased tin, touching each other. Cover and prove for 30 to 40 minutes until puffed.

Heat the oven to 190 C (170 C fan). Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden. Mix the icing sugar with just enough water (about 2 tablespoons) to make a thin glacé icing. Drizzle over the buns while they are still warm. Pull apart to serve.
